_meta.purpose: Regular-pass MODERNIZATION overlay — the 'every beat gets dressed up' layer. Each entry names a STORY_SCENES sceneKey + act phase and adds cosmetic narration: a speaker nameplate, a tone (drives the speaker-plate accent colour via _actAccentForTone), an optional appended sensory/atmosphere line, and an optional pure-FLAVOR choice (no mechanical effect). Applied at load by _applyStoryFraming AFTER interactions, and it only fills gaps — it never overrides an act that already has an interaction / branches / authored choice. Ships here as data so the modernization pass never edits the 4MB STORY_SCENES literal and stays fully reviewable + revertible.
_meta.shape: { sceneKey, phase, speaker?:'Name', tone?:'cold|villain|dread|grief|mystery|rival|warm|hope|calm|eerie|tender', spriteSide?:'left|right', appendLines?:[..], choice?:{ persistKey, options:[{label,value,reply:[..]}] }, label? }
_meta.tones: warm gold · villain/anger red · dread/eerie/horror violet · mystery lilac · rival/cold blue · grief/sorrow slate · hope green · calm/tender teal

options.label: Remember the plate
reply: You say it once under your breath and once to yourself, to see if you still have it.

options.label: Let the truck go
reply: The driver nods when you step back. He probably makes that face at every stop.

options.label: Walk beside the cart
reply: The driver shifts over to give you the good part of the road. Up at the hill he nods once before he reaches for the latch.

options.label: Give them the road
reply: You wait by the gate with your hand on it. The Marowak is close enough for you to hear the dirt shift under its feet.

options.label: Read every first name
reply: You read until the engineer takes his glasses off. The last name is short. There’s a blank half page below it.

options.label: Close the ledger
reply: You close it and keep a finger on the page. The engineer fetches an envelope.

options.label: Put the belt back
reply: The buckle rests in a clean mark on the felt. You fit it into the mark.

options.label: Look under the buckle
reply: There’s a flake of gold lettering under the clasp. When you put it back, it sticks to your thumb.

inject.speaker: Magma Preacher
appendLines: The empty can scrapes the bottom of the streambed when its owner sets it down.

options.label: Take down the flag
reply: The rope is warm where it led into the well. You fold the flag and set it under the bucket.

options.label: Leave the flag
reply: You step around the bucket. The rope makes a sound against the rim when the flag moves.

appendLines: The ground shifts under his knees. He waits for it to settle before he goes on.

options.label: Tell him about the houses downhill
reply: “I know which houses,” Maxie says. He lists the first three. He knows them all.

options.label: Wait for him to finish
reply: He moves his hand close to the stone before he starts again. You wait well back from the edge.

appendLines: On his way in, the instructor nudges a broken bottle out of the shallows with his heel.

options.label: Put a hand in the current
reply: A pebble rolls past your thumb and takes the sand from under it. The instructor watches you pull back.

options.label: Stay on the bank
reply: A child spots you and puts one hand up to wave. The instructor tells them to use both hands to swim.

appendLines: The masonry grinds against itself as each wave comes through.

options.label: Offer Archie a hand
reply: He looks at your hand. “Move back a step,” he says, and places his foot where you were standing.

options.label: Stay on the dry stones
reply: You keep clear of the breach. He tests the next foothold, doesn’t find one and tries it again.

inject.speaker: Galactic Grunt
appendLines: One light over the kiosk is humming. The volunteer puts another cup out beneath it.

options.label: Ask about the circled date
reply: She reads it out and adds that you’ll need a watch to notice the exact time. You ask her whose watch she’ll use.

options.label: Leave the book with her
reply: She closes it on her pencil so she can get back to the page. The stars are where they were a minute ago.

appendLines: A moth bats once against the seam and comes out on the other side of your shadow.

options.label: Ask who asked him
reply: Cyrus starts to give you a name. He gets as far as the first sound before the seam opens another inch.

options.label: Climb past him
reply: Your boot rests beside the lip of the seam. Below it, the porch light has gone out.

inject.speaker: Plasma Sage
appendLines: The kid’s shoes have already soaked through. They try to stand on the dry edge of a leaf.

options.label: Read the donor card
reply: A family has dedicated the release to their old partner. You can see the child’s writing through the back of the card.

options.label: Watch the loading dock
reply: A handler counts the crates back in. Whoever wrote the donation receipt counted out the same number.

options.label: Take the final page
reply: You ease it out so the next page stays in the binding. Time has left the words from the removed sheet impressed on it.

options.label: Leave the book in place
reply: The ribbon still marks the page he came back to. You close it on the ribbon.

inject.speaker: Flare Grunt
appendLines: His left lens is tinted a little darker than the right.

options.label: Sit at the kitchen table
reply: The knife is still by the slice of bread. Someone scraped the last of the butter into one corner of the dish.

options.label: Close the doors
reply: Most of them still latch. One opens again before you reach the curb.

options.label: Stay for your name
reply: The reader says it right on the first try. Nobody sitting near you turns round.

options.label: Leave before they read it
reply: You get as far as the alley while they’re still reading the block before yours. The speaker reaches you there too.

options.label: Leave a coin behind it
reply: You tuck the coin through the bottom tear. The front lies a little flatter against the fence.

options.label: Photograph the front
reply: In the picture the two letters match perfectly. You close it before anyone asks what you’re looking at.

options.label: Walk down the block with them
reply: You carry the loose drawers while they drag it. At the corner they ask which drawer used to hold the oranges.

options.label: Give them space
reply: From the curb you hear the front feet hit the second step. Someone opens a gate along the street.

appendLines: The speakers on the steps are off. Somebody has left their cables coiled across the doorway.

options.label: Offer Impidimp a hand
reply: It puts one finger around yours. Marnie can take her sleeve back now. She leaves it where it is.

options.label: Let them sit together
reply: Marnie frees the cuff with her other hand so the Impidimp can get a better grip.

options.label: Ask what the money is for
reply: He tells you to ask the organizer, who has already gone through the door. “Stick around,” he says. “He’ll be back for more.”

options.label: Read the envelope
reply: Beneath STREET TEAM someone has stamped a date three weeks ahead. You’ve seen it on the tickets.

appendLines: The painter leaves one handprint where he steadies himself against the wall.

options.label: Keep the letter
reply: You fold the crest in half so it fits in your pocket. The contract goes untouched back into the envelope.

options.label: Read through the offer
reply: The last page gives them permission to write your statement if you resign. The word voluntarily is already filled in.

options.label: Keep standing
reply: Rose leaves the other chair close to the window. He has to stand up to point at the darker blocks too.

options.label: Sit and hear him out
reply: Rose gives you the seat from which you can see the outages. For a moment you watch the same street.

options.label: Copy the teachers’ names
reply: You get to the last one before the caretaker asks what class you’re looking for. You tell her you’ve found it.

options.label: Leave the board alone
reply: One of the corners is loose. You push the pin back in far enough to keep that sheet from falling.

options.label: Read the whole letter
reply: The final sentence thanks the staff for everything they did during a difficult period. You can hear the last class of the day letting out as you read.

options.label: Leave the letter on the desk
reply: The nameplate still has tape over the first letter of the name. A caretaker asks for a moment to finish changing it.

appendLines: The teacher doesn’t have to prompt the line about coming home.

options.label: Check the wet crate
reply: The broker moves his scale on top of it. Through a gap in the wood you see enough to know which way the bone was put in.

options.label: Keep walking
reply: The scale clicks again before you reach the turn. Nobody calls after you.

options.label: Check the length
reply: You set the heel of your boot at one end. At the other end your shadow falls just short.

options.label: Leave Marowak to dig
reply: As you start back downhill, the first stroke of the club lands deeper than the rest.

appendLines: The shop closed for the festival three weeks ago. The poster has since faded right behind the mask.

options.label: Keep looking
reply: The eye lines don’t match the ones in the reflection. You move first so you’ll know who moved.

options.label: Step away from the glass
reply: Your reflection passes across the costume on the way out. The face stays where it was.

options.label: Leave some change
reply: She puts the coins next to her tea. She hasn’t asked whose they are.

options.label: Keep your coins
reply: She brings the cup up with both hands and holds it there until the next game begins.

appendLines: The latest tape is still clear. You can see the yellowed tape beneath it.

options.label: Call to the children
reply: The one in the middle loosens their grip. The others wait before they step again.

options.label: Let them pass
reply: The coats make the same sound going round the bend as they did coming straight toward you.

options.label: Touch your name
reply: The pressure of the pen has gone through to the next sheet. There’s already a line for somebody else beneath it.

options.label: Close the binder
reply: The lid stays up over your finger. It closes the rest of the way only after you pull back.

appendLines: A grain of gravel is wedged in the buckle.

options.label: Hum the next line
reply: For two notes you sing it together. At the third, one of you stops. Neither can say which.

options.label: Ask about the weather
reply: They put on their packed coat without realizing they’d been folding it. The question is forgotten by the time they leave.

options.label: Stay by the blank stone
reply: You sit long enough to hear your partner settle on the far side. No one comes to ask you to leave.

options.label: Leave it in place
reply: The Phantump shifts the stone a little to let the rain reach its top. You go back through the gap in the trees.

appendLines: Rain has erased the corner with the brightest cheek.

options.label: Fix the loose corner
reply: The tape lets go with a bit of bark. You press it down somewhere smooth and keep your thumb on it until the paper stays.

options.label: Leave the drawing alone
reply: From a little way down the road you can still see the two taped ears above the grass.

options.label: Sit in the next seat
reply: The player shows you the cup. When you push one coin across, they slip it into a pocket instead of the machine.

options.label: Find an attendant
reply: When you get back with the attendant, the seat is empty. The machine has stopped with one coin sticking out.

appendLines: The child has put an empty hand out to balance.

options.label: Tie the mitten where someone will see it
reply: You fix it to the fence with the cuff facing up. It hangs still in the wind.

options.label: Take the mitten with you
reply: You make room in the dry pocket. It’s the only thing in it when you zip it shut.

options.label: Leave a message below it
reply: You write, “If the wind picks up, take somebody’s hand.” The corner of the page comes away under your pen.

options.label: Leave the drawing as it is
reply: A teacher straightens the page at the end of the line. Everyone in the hall keeps passing it on their way out.

appendLines: A grain of wet dirt stays stuck to the cap when the head turns.

options.label: Write in the margin
reply: You add, “It kept going long after the bug stopped.” There’s only enough pencil space for one more word.

options.label: Leave the guide open
reply: You move the paperweight away from the pencil marks so the next reader can see them.

options.label: Wake the puppeteer
reply: He rubs his eyes and asks whether they made it all the way to the end. The small one at the curtain turns around.

options.label: Leave before the curtain
reply: You get to the door before the applause. From the hall you hear a little wooden hand clap a little late.

appendLines: The fabric is colder than the dirt. It takes a moment to get the mud out of the stitches.

options.label: Keep the patch
reply: You carry it in a different pocket from the map. Some wet soil falls out while you close it.

options.label: Put it back in the dirt
reply: You turn the patch so the number can’t be seen from the path. A few of the new stitches still show.

options.label: Try the latch
reply: The latch gives a little. Behind the window, the third sheet settles forward by itself.

options.label: Leave the case shut
reply: You turn the case so the reflection takes the writing away. It won’t be visible from the trail anymore.
